analysis.title: the more we look at tech the less we understand
key_insights: Tech charts give conflicting signals: AI earnings growth and fund manager positioning are bullish, while valuations, weakening breadth and a semis losing streak are bearish. The note offers no resolution and says several different things may be happening at once.

Apple has reached a $5 trillion market cap intraday on six different days but has not closed above it. Goldman's Peter Callahan reads the rally as defensive, citing the rolling 22-day correlation between Apple and the NDX.
Apple trades at nearly 11x sales, the highest valuation in the company's history (Bilello).
Semiconductors have fallen six consecutive sessions, their longest losing streak in 17 months.
Per Citadel, Micron and Nvidia alone are expected to account for 36% of S&P 500 earnings growth in Q3.
BofA FMS: the share of fund managers overweight tech rose to 37% from 30% a month earlier, the highest since August 2020.
Deutsche Bank is tactically cautious on tech. It argues the latest rotation into the sector is approaching exhaustion and that tech is very close to the upper end of its long-term trend channel.
Todd Sohn: tech exposure in the S&P 500 is almost larger than all the cyclical sectors combined.
Nvidia, Apple, Alphabet and Microsoft account for roughly 33% of the S&P 500, up from 9% in 2015. Their average three-month correlation has fallen to 3.8%.
The spread between the Nasdaq 100 and Russell 2000 50-DMAs is in the 99th percentile of readings (Bespoke).
Six-month correlations of SMH and QQQ with changes in S&P 500 breadth are at their lowest in about 20 years (SMH -0.12, QQQ +0.02).
Tuesday was the 32nd straight session in which the Nasdaq had more new 52-week lows than new highs, the longest streak since April 2025 (Neil Sethi).

Fidelity says the AI-versus-dot-com price analog has reached the climax of the 1998-2000 internet bubble analog. It expects the analog to fail sooner or later, possibly sooner given the valuation difference.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning is crowded and breadth is weak, but AI earnings growth is strong. The note gives no directional call.
Semis are on a six-session losing streak, with two names expected to drive 36% of S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth.

earnings_insights: Citadel: Micron and Nvidia are expected to account for 36% of S&P 500 earnings growth in Q3 (estimate, not a reported figure).
risk_factors: Concentration: Nvidia, Apple, Alphabet and Microsoft are about 33% of the S&P 500, and two semiconductor names are expected to drive 36% of Q3 earnings growth.
Deteriorating market breadth alongside the highest tech overweight among fund managers since 2020.
Tech near the upper end of its long-term trend channel (Deutsche Bank).
Apple's valuation of nearly 11x sales is a record for the company.
Fidelity's dot-com analog has reached the climax of the 1998-2000 bubble comparison.

Chart of total return for S&P 500 semiconductor vs. software stocks since the ChatGPT launch on Nov 30, 2022 (Deutsche Bank). The text gives no values.
Fidelity chart of the AI-versus-dot-com analog, described in the text as at the climax of the 1998-2000 internet bubble analog.

The Nasdaq has posted 32 straight sessions with more new 52-week lows than new highs, the longest streak since April 2025.
